GB.label: 11:52 Navan
GB.race: Kilberry Pub & Kitchen Maiden Hurdle (Turf) 4YO+ 2m 4f 50y Winner: €9,000 (22 runners)
GB.going: Hurdle: Good To Yielding Yielding In Places; Chase: Yielding Good To Yielding In Places
GB.note: CHARISMATIC KID is the one to beat on bumper form, and he may well make a winning start over hurdles. The main danger looks to be Willie Mullins' The Irish Avatar, who was useful in his own right in bumpers. OutofAfrika, Luxor Love and Confidence Within are others to note.

runners.tf_comment: Crystal Ocean gelding. Half-brother to fair hurdler Apples Jane, stays 2½m. Dam (Apple's Jade) prolific Grade 1 winning hurdler at up to 3m. From a family connections have enjoyed plenty of success with. Market likely to guide expectations for this interesting newcomer.

€25,000 3-y-o, £1,000 5-y-o, Shirocco gelding. Closely related to useful hurdler Lucky Road. Dam, lightly raced in points, half-sister to top-class chaser (stayed 25f) Road To Respect. Third completed start in points, again fell last time (Apr 2026). Probably one for the longer term under Rules.

Runner-up on completed start in points (May 2026). Sent off at long odds and duly went with little encouragement on hurdling bow at Fairyhouse (2m) 11 days ago. Likely a handicap project now up in trip off a fairly quick turnaround.

€60,000 3-y-o, Walk In The Park gelding. Half-brother to useful hurdler/high-class chaser Dunvegan. Well-related sort who got off the mark at the fourth attempt in points (May 2026). Charismatic Kid looks stable's leading hope on jockey bookings.

Picked up for £300,000 by powerful connections after winning on debut. Still green when third in a Leopardstown Grade 2 before producing one of the best bumper performances of the season at Fairyhouse in April. Exciting hurdling debutant who may prove a cut above these (tongue strap on first time).

€20,000 3-y-o, Mahler gelding. Brother to fairly useful hurdler/useful chaser Tightenourbelts, and half-brother to 4 winners, including fairly useful hurdler Miss Goldfire. Runner-up completed start in points. Possibly amiss at Gowran on Rules debut (12/1). Likely one for handicaps now.

Looked a useful prospect when off the mark in a Kilbeggan bumper on debut, going with enthusiasm/winning easily. Didn't hit the same heights when 15-length third on hurdling bow at Listowel in late-September, but he's entitled to do better stepping up in trip.
In frame both completed starts in points in 2025. Only showed a bit more than on Rules debut at Tramore (2m) in April. Up in trip and this looks a springboard to handicaps.
Made little appeal on paper and shaped accordingly in a Punchestown bumper in April. Hard to be confident of better now up in trip for hurdling bow.
Runner-up sole start in points. Well held 3 starts under Rules to date. Needs this run for a mark.
Point winner who was well held in a pair of maiden hurdles for Colin A. McBratney. New connections likely have one eye on handicaps.
€18,000 3-y-o, Walzertakt gelding. Brother to fair hurdler/chase winner Kalista Love, stays 25f. Off mark in points at second attempt (Feb 2026). Has to be respected now hurdling for excellent yard.

€68,000 3-y-o, Order of St George gelding. Half-brother to 3 winners, including high-class but temperamental hurdler Labaik and fairly useful hurdler Aiguille Rouge. Placed once from 4 starts in points. Yard knows this family well and he's likely one for down the line.

€25,000 3-y-o. Shirocco gelding. Half-brother to bumper winners Tiger Bay Queen/Inion Tiogair. Dam fair 3m hurdle winner. Easily won sole start in British points. Fairly useful winner second of 3 bumper starts last season. Respected up in trip on hurdles bow, though work to do with Charismatic Kid.
Showed more than first time up at Wexford last month, though still faces a tall order in a maiden hurdle of this calibre.

One-time fairly useful Flat performer. Has shown little in 2 starts in that sphere since returning from a 3-year absence. Given a considerate introduction to hurdling 6 days ago and makes little appeal this side of handicaps.

Soldier of Fortune gelding. Dam, placed on second of 2 starts over hurdles in France, half-sister to smart hurdler/chaser (17f-21f winner) Le Tranquille and fairly useful hurdler/useful chaser (stays 3m) Karl Philippe. Looks down the Gordon Elliott pecking order on jockey bookings.

Bought for £200,000 after finishing runner-up sole outing in points. Made a winning Rules debut at Navan before disappointing in Champion Bumper. Still rough around the edges when 8½ lengths fifth in Punchestown Grade 1. Looks the part and may well improve now hurdling for leading yard.
Made frame completed start in points (May 2026). Ran to a modest level when beaten 16½ lengths on hurdling debut at Down Royal (2¾m). Stable again has better-fancied runners.

Australia gelding. Half-brother to fair hurdler Janes Harbour. Dam (h80), lightly raced over hurdles, 1½m winner on Flat, half-sister to French hurdler (stayed 19f) For Fun out of French hurdler (2¼m winner) Funny Feerie. Probably a longer-term project for capable stable.
Made frame sole start in points prior to showing some promise in a couple of bumpers. Looked one for later on when down the field on hurdling debut at Fairyhouse (2m) 11 days ago.
Useful Flat performer who has been brought along quietly in 3 maiden hurdle starts to date. Ought to get a mark after this run and one to note for handicaps.

GB.label: 13:02 Navan
GB.race: Hotel Park St. Johann In Tirol Austria Handicap Hurdle (Turf) 4YO+ 2m 50y Winner: €12,000 (16 runners)
GB.going: Hurdle: Good To Yielding Yielding In Places; Chase: Yielding Good To Yielding In Places
GB.note: SOMMESKY looked sure to win when falling at the last at Punchestown last season and, having been given plenty of time to get over that misfortune, is fancied to make amends despite his lengthy absence. Rightfolksplease has returned better than ever since joining his new yard with back-to-back wins in August and looks the main threat, with both Radiator Springs and Arch Empire also capable of being in the mix.

runners.tf_comment: Without a win since spring 2025 but shaped much better than the bare result when 12½ lengths ninth of 12 to Stuntman Steve at Down Royal a fortnight ago, second and staying on well just over a length behind the winner when chance-ending mistake last. Claims if putting in a clear round of jumping.
Well backed/much improved to make a winning handicap debut in a 13-runner event at Clonmel (2m, soft) in April. Hasn't kicked on from that since, though, and his current mark demands improvement.

Landed 2m Wexford maiden before following up in 12-runner C&D handicap at Navan 4 days later, both in March. Stiff task on final start. Will be suited by the return to handicap company but may need the run after 6 months off and current mark demands a resumption of progress.

Latest win in handicap hurdle at Wexford last season. Third in handicap chases on both completed starts since. Returns from 173-day break back over hurdles and remains on a handy mark based on the pick of last season's efforts over fences.

Landed back-to-back handicap hurdles at Naas in February 2025, but failed to fire on both subsequent outings that year and hasn't offered much encouragement in a handful of starts on the level since returning to action in July.

Useful 3-time Cartmel winner. Career-best success in big-field handicap at Galway Festival in August. Below that form since and the likelihood is he'll need to be better than ever if he's to secure a seventh career success here.
Proved a different proposition when running out a convincing winner of Naas handicap (2m heavy) last season, but has struggled off higher marks since, including on return in October.

Smooth-travelling type who resumed winning ways back in a less competitive race at Downpatrick (2¼m, good) in August. Has shaped as if still in form on both outings since, needing more of an end-to-end gallop when 7¼ lengths fifth of 12 to Stuntman Steve at Down Royal 14 days ago.
Bordering on smart chaser at best but hasn't won since the autumn of 2024 and there's been little sign of an imminent return to form in handicap hurdles on his last 2 starts.

Low-mileage point winner who was successful on second hurdle start at Clonmel last season. Has shaped as if ahead of her mark on 2 of her 3 handicap outings since, including when ¾-length fourth of 18 to Fraher Field at Listowel in September, collared late on after making effort earlier than ideal.

Smooth-travelling type who returned from a lay-off better than ever for present yard. Justified support to complete a quick-fire double under this good-value claimer (2-2) at Tramore in August. Presumably been freshened up and bold bid expected on hat-trick attempt.
Point winner. Confirmed previous promise when winning mares maiden hurdle at Galway by 6 lengths from Light Up The Dark. Opening mark demands improvement on handicap debut, though.
Won maiden chase at Roscommon last summer but has failed to progress in handicaps since, including when last seen at Wexford last time.

Was 3 lengths clear and in the process of showing much improved form when falling at the last in a handicap hurdle won by Linden Arden at Punchestown 11 months ago. Not seen since but must be considered off same mark with an additional 7 lb being claimed by his conditional rider.

A 3-time course winner, including twice over C&D, the latest of those wins coming on heavy ground around this time last year. Largely out of form since but entitled to be sharper for last month's return and no surprise were he to return to form back at this venue. Blinkers back on.

Bumper winner/useful on Flat who made an encouraging start over hurdles when fifth at Roscommon back in 2023. Lightly raced in this sphere since, but may do better now tackling a handicap with a hood applied. One to note if market speaks in his favour.

GB.label: 13:35 Navan
GB.race: Bar 1 Betting 'Download Our App' for Auction Novice Hurdle (Grade 3) (Class 1) (Turf) 4YO+ 2m 50y Winner: €25,199 (8 runners)
GB.going: Hurdle: Good To Yielding Yielding In Places; Chase: Yielding Good To Yielding In Places
GB.note: THINKITDONTJINXIT made an impressive start over hurdles at Galway last month, travelling and jumping well before quickening clear from the home turn, and he is fancied to cope with the step up in grade, with City of Cork feared most after creating a taking impression on his return at Clonmel and hurdling debutant It's Only A Game and recent Gowran scorer The Captain's Word also respected.

runners.tf_comment: Confirmed promise of hurdling debut and a couple of in-frame bumper efforts when winning 17f maiden hurdle at Clonmel last month. Steps up in grade now but looks open to further progress.

Brother to useful hurdler Sixandahalf. Won a bumper at Ballinrobe in May and then followed up back over hurdles when landing 15-runner maiden hurdle at Punchestown in October. Open to further improvement.

Underlined a bright start over hurdles when landing the odds in Wexford maiden in August and then showed further progress when following up in a listed 4-y-o handicap at Listowel in September. Best excused latest Flat outing but lacks the potential of some of these now tackling a Grade 3 novice.

Won Punchestown bumper last season before being highly tried in Grade 2 event there and in Champion Bumper at Cheltenham. Very much the type to do better now hurdling and shrewd yard is not normally one to fire an arrow at a target it has no hope of hitting. Wears first-time hood. Interesting.

Didn't need to replicate the fairly useful form he's shown on the Flat to make a winning debut over hurdles when landing a maiden at Ballinrobe in May. Arrives fit and in-form from the Flat and is entitled to progress in this sphere but looks a big ask.

Fairly useful bumper winner that hasn't always looked the most straightforward of characters but made an encouraging start to life over hurdles, getting off the mark at the second attempt in this sphere when comfortably landing a Fairyhouse maiden last month.

Made frame both starts in points and in a bumper prior to narrowly winning 20-runner maiden hurdle at Gowran in October by a nose from next-time-out winner Lirakali. Faces a much tougher test now upped in grade but there's clearly better still to come.

Point winner who showed above-average bumper form and made a striking hurdles debut when routing 19 rivals by 11 lengths at Galway last month. From a yard with a good record in this race, he looks to hold strong claims with further improvement likely.

GB.label: 14:07 Navan
GB.race: Railway Bar Lismullen Hurdle (Grade 2) (Class 1) (Turf) 4YO+ 2m 4f 50y Winner: €42,000 (8 runners)
GB.going: Hurdle: Good To Yielding Yielding In Places; Chase: Yielding Good To Yielding In Places
GB.note: SLADE STEEL has not progressed as hoped since his 2024 Supreme success, but his return to hurdles when last seen duly sparked a revival and he is fancied to make a winning reappearance. The Yellow Clay is a smart hurdler with a good course record to his name and is feared most, with Feet of A Dancer also very much respected due to her excellent record when fresh.

runners.tf_comment: Progressive last season, winning 3 times and also placed in Galway Hurdle and the December Hurdle. Had excuses when failing to fire in latest renewal of Galway Hurdle in July but has stamina to prove at this trip and Jack Kennedy prefers The Yellow Clay.

Dual hurdles winner now better known as a smart staying handicapper on the Flat, having produced his best effort since the previous year’s renewal when third in last month’s Cesarewitch at Newmarket; reverts to hurdling for the first time in 2 years, so the market should prove highly informative.

Reliable sort has won on return in each of her last 3 seasons and registered her first graded success when landing Yorkshire Rose at Doncaster (3m). Followed that with a good third of 7 to Wodhooh in David Nicholson Mares' Hurdle at Cheltenham. Yard is in good form and she must be respected.

Very smart stayer that has twice won this race in the past and added the Galmoy, Stayers’ and Liverpool Hurdles to his record last season. Has a fine record fresh but shoulders a Grade 1 penalty here and goes without J. J. Slevin, who has been on board for 10 of his last 11 wins. Blinkers off.

Dual bumper winner who made up into a smart novice hurdler last season, winning 4 times, including a Grade 3 this course before providing his owner/trainer with first Grade 1 success at Naas. Ran well when fifth to King Rasko Grey at Cheltenham when last seen and steps into open graded company now.

Belatedly added to his 2024 Supreme Hurdle success when landing the Ballybrin Hurdle at Fairyhouse in April by 1¾ lengths from Kawaboomga. Has won over C&D and boasts a solid record fresh and must be considered with the yard going well.

Got stalling career back on track over hurdles last season, winning 3 times, including Grade 2 Boyne Hurdle at this course in February. Has run poorly on both outings since, again looking less than straightforward back over fences when last seen. Smart on his day but comes with risks attached.

Smart hurdler who won over C&D twice as a novice but was slightly underwhelming stepping into open company last season, his sole placing coming when turned over at odds on in this race. Well suited by the conditions this time around, though, and should be firmly in the mix if at his best.

GB.label: 14:43 Navan
GB.race: Bar 1 Betting Fortria Chase (Grade 2) (Class 1) (Turf) 5YO+ 2m Winner: €42,000 (7 runners)
GB.going: Hurdle: Good To Yielding Yielding In Places; Chase: Yielding Good To Yielding In Places
GB.note: ONLY BY NIGHT boasts an excellent record fresh and, while not at the same level as an on-song Majborough, looks worth chancing against that enigmatic but talented rival in a race where any jumping flaw could prove costly. Solness rates best of the rest.

runners.tf_comment: Smart chaser who cosily landed 11-runner handicap chase at Galway (2¼m, good to soft) in August. Better effort since when chasing home Fleur In The Park in PWC Champion Chase at Gowran last month. Career best needed in this company, though.

High-class chaser that has won the last 2 renewals of this race and managed to beat an underperforming and returning Majborough in the Hilly Way at Cork last December. Has been disappointing since, though, and hopes very much pinned on a 6-month break and return to this venue sparking a revival.
Point and maiden hurdle winner who has been placed on all 5 starts in handicap chases but is flying far too high in this company.

Top-class chaser capable of devastating displays of dominance, as he showed in last season’s Dublin Chase, but his jumping has too often been his undoing and, while anything close to his best should suffice, finding an early rhythm will be crucial.

Classy mare who was just touched off in the 2025 Arkle before landing the Grade 3 Poplar Square Chase at Naas and finishing second in the Grade 2 Mrs Paddy Power Mares Chase at Cheltenham last season. Boasts excellent record fresh and suited by the race conditions. Major player.

High-class chaser who gained a third Leopardstown Grade 1 win over Christmas and ran at least as well when narrowly denied by Grey Dawning in the Melling Chase at Aintree; a recent Flat win confirms his well-being and he commands respect, though he’s unlikely to get his own way out in front.

Smart chaser who didn't kick on stepping into open company last season but posted his best effort of the campaign when chasing home Blood Destiny in a Grade 3 event at Naas in February. Has disappointed on both starts since, though, and this looks a stiff task.

GB.label: 15:18 Navan
GB.race: Jimmy & Sheila Owens Irish EBF Beginners Chase (Turf) 4YO+ 2m 1f Winner: €9,900 (11 runners)
GB.going: Hurdle: Good To Yielding Yielding In Places; Chase: Yielding Good To Yielding In Places
GB.note: This is often a very informative maiden chase and this year's looks no different. MIGHTY PARK was held back by inexperience in the Supreme following his demolition job on his Fairyhouse hurdling debut and looks one to follow over fences this season. He can get his chasing career off to the perfect start, perhaps at the expense of his stablemate Saint Baco, who could well be suited by the drop back in trip on first go over the larger obstacles. Largy Star and Bleu De Vassy also deserve mentions.

runners.tf_comment: Took 4 goes to get off the mark in bumpers but hit the ground running over hurdles, showing useful form when winning first 2 starts in 2024/25, including Navan Grade 3. Had an off-day when well beaten in Leopardstown Grade 1 when last seen later that season but still an interesting chasing debutant.

Bumper winner who overcame a late blunder to open his hurdle account in 2m maiden at Gowran in January. Went backwards from a considerate chasing debut when a well-held fourth at Naas in March, though, and probably more one for handicaps in this sphere.

Looked a different proposition when winning 21-runner handicap hurdle at Fairyhouse (2m, soft) in April. Clearly not 100% on the day when dropping away quickly at Punchestown later that month and is not without interest now going chasing being a point winner.
Put both his point and hurdle experience to good use to land 21-runner bumper at Punchestown (19f, good to soft) in May. Interesting now switching to chasing after just 3 starts under Rules.

Closely related to King George winner/Cheltenham Gold Cup runner-up Might Bite. Made a striking winning start to his hurdle career when making all by a wide margin at Fairyhouse in January. Held back by inexperience in the Supreme on only outing since and is a most interesting chasing prospect.

Progressive hurdler who made it 3 wins from 5 starts in handicap company in 24-runner event at Punchestown (19f, good to soft) in late-April. Strong-travelling type who must enter calculations on chasing debut.

Pulled up sole outing in points but was set to make it 2-2 in handicap hurdles when falling at Fairyhouse in April. However, went amiss at Cork the following month and went with no encouragement on last week's chasing debut at Naas.

Half-brother to yard's high-class jumper Saint Roi and landed the odds in 2m maiden hurdle at Navan on yard debut in December. Found life tougher at a higher level thereafter but not disgraced in Grade 1 at Punchestown on final outing and looks interesting dropping back in trip for chase debut.

A lightly-raced winner over hurdles who seemed to pay for an aggressive ride returning from a 4-month absence when 29 lengths third of 4 on chasing debut at Killarney (21f) in early-October. Drop back in trip looks a positive and should leave that form well behind.

Showed useful form when placed all 4 starts in maidens last season. Failed to see his race out back in a handicap at Punchestown when last seen at the beginning of May and probably vulnerable, for all that he sets the standard on return to maiden company.
Fair winner over hurdles but went with no encouragement in 2 maiden chases last November. Has left P. J. Rothwell.

GB.label: 15:53 Navan
GB.race: Bar 1 Betting Best Odds Guaranteed Overnight (Pro/Am) Flat Race (Turf) 4YO+ 2m 50y Winner: €9,000 (10 runners)
GB.going: Hurdle: Good To Yielding Yielding In Places; Chase: Yielding Good To Yielding In Places
GB.note: A bumper that Gordon Elliott has tended to target over the years and the pick of his trio looks to be £310,000 winning pointer UNCLE PAD, who hammered a rival in his point that has since made an encouraging hurdling debut. Kanzler represents the mighty Willie Mullins and is feared most, with his lengthy absence since winning a point of no real concern given his connections. Airforce Marshal beat a subsequent winner under Rules when landing his point and is also respected.

runners.tf_comment: £50,000 5-y-o, fifth foal, closely related to fairly useful hurdler/chaser Well Dick (29f winner, by Well Chosen), and half-brother to winning hurdler by Shantou. Dam, unraced, sister to ungenuine but fairly useful hurdler/chaser up to 3m Its Crucial. Form of point win looks strong.

£75,000 3-y-o, £170,000 4-y-o. Off mark on second start in points (May 2026). Half-brother to dual bumper winner Luttrell Lad (stayed 2¾m) out of a 2½m staying mare. In very capable hands (one of 3 Elliott runners).
First foal, dam, bumper/21f hurdle winner (stayed 23f), sister to useful hurdler (stayed 25f) Teescomponents Lad and fairly useful hurdler/fair chaser (stays 21f) Teescomponentsyess.
Third foal, dam unraced. Fell both starts in points in early-2026.
£165,000 4-y-o, fourth foal, dam 10.5f winner in Germany. Comfortable winner sole start in points (Feb 2025). Long absence rarely a concern for all-conquering yard. Wears hood.
Best effort in bumpers (modest form) when 12¾ lengths fifth of 7 at Limerick last season. Returns from 7-month absence.

Order of St George gelding who produced a promising first effort when staying on for second in an 11-runner bumper at Leopardstown (2m) last December, no match for the winner but nicely clear of the remainder. Open to improvement on return from 11 months off.
Order of St George gelding. Looked as if in need of more time when well held in bumper at Punchestown in April.
Placed all 4 starts in bumpers, finding only one too good on his last 3, beaten 7½ lengths by Green Hint in 13-runner event at Listowel on latest.

Vadamos gelding. Closely related to French hurdler/chaser Sorcier du Roi, and half-sister to 3 winners, including fairly useful hurdler/chaser Hello Sweetie. Easy winner of sole outing in points and bought for £310,000 after, so of obvious interest, especially having joined top stable.

GB.label: 12:07 Uttoxeter
GB.race: Quinnbet Conditional Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle (Class 5) (Turf) 3YO+ 2m 3f 207y Winner: £3,697 (8 runners)
GB.note: SPARTAN TIMES returns from a short break with his yard continuing in excellent order and given there's still scope from his current mark based on his Flat form, he could be the answer. Lunar Orbit and French recruit Zeus Forlonge head the opposition.

runners.tf_comment: Scored twice at up to 2½m over hurdles last summer. Back to form when second over hurdles at Worcester (23f) in August but looks one with problems suddenly judged on next 3 efforts.

Ground-versatile sort who won 4 times around 2½m last season. Hard to derive much promise from his first 3 outings this autumn but eased a further 2 lb and much more like it when second of 8 at Worcester 3 weeks ago. Cheekpieces back on.

Fairly useful on the Flat. Justified support to land a Market Rasen juvenile in December. Runner-up twice for Dan Skelton, latterly when displaying improved form against a thriving rival at Hereford 3 weeks ago. Has to command respect but he can pull hard so no easy ride for a conditional.

Successful between the flags and handicap debut fourth of 15 at Newcastle in February was a step in the right direction. Fitted with a tongue tie when third over 23f at Bangor in March, seeing it out well. Off since and yard yet to fully fire this season.
Progressive form in a trio of maiden hurdles in Ireland for Edward F. Power this summer. Moved yards ahead of this handicap debut but mark demands that he continues to improve.

Shrugged off any element of rustiness with a battling display when making a winning handicap debut here in May (2m). Runner-up twice on the level since and possible excuse for both efforts in this sphere, reportedly finishing lame in September. Given a break and yard in form.

Low-mileage 6-y-o who produced an improved effort in first-time cheekpieces when runner-up at Hereford (2m) in May. Easy to back when failing to reproduce that form at Stratford but returned from 5 months off minus cheekpieces with a sound effort at that venue. Headgear back on.
Half-brother to 7 winners and claimed on the back of an improved showing when runner-up at Auteuil in May. Upped slightly in trip and has to command serious respect given the yard he's joined.

GB.label: 12:42 Uttoxeter
GB.race: Somersby Novices' Hurdle (Gbb Race) (Class 4) (Turf) 4YO+ 1m 7f 168y Winner: £5,446 (9 runners)
GB.note: Bumper/hurdles winner SPANISH DARLING didn't look out of place when fourth pitched into a Grade 2 on just his second hurdles start at Cheltenham 3 weeks ago, within a length of the lead prior to fluffing his lines at the last. Firmly remaining with his best days ahead of him, he's impossible to oppose returned to much calmer waters. Bumper winner Port Isaac and newcomers Made For Mary and Montevallo may emerge next best.

runners.tf_comment: Fair winner up to 1m on all-weather this year but ended the season on a low-key note and at long odds, he went with no promise when pulled up in a C&D novice on hurdles debut 7 days ago.

Maiden pointer who exceeded expectations on Rules debut when fourth of 12 in maiden chase at Kilbeggan (2½m) in June. However, couldn't replicate that when well held over hurdles at Roscommon on final start for Donncha Duggan in August. Made an interesting yard switch but possibly one for later on.

Fair form when winning first of 2 starts in bumpers initially this season. Related to several hurdle winners but fitted with a hood, she was given a considerate introduction when fourth in a mares maiden (17f) at Newton Abbot in July. This promises to reveal more now debuting for new yard.

€24,000 3-y-o, Blue Bresil filly. Dam (b89), point/bumper winner, half-sister to winning hurdler/top-class chaser (stays 3¼m) Conflated. Pedigree offers hope debuting for stable who continue amongst the winners and support behind her would look interesting.

€52,000 3-y-o, Maxios gelding. Dam (c124/h112) 2½m/21f hurdle/chase winner (stayed 23f). Made frame both starts in Irish points, runner-up last time (Feb 2026) and worth noting if supported in the betting ahead of Rules/hurdles debut.

Linda's Lad gelding who got off the mark in points at second attempt in May but went off a big price and showed nothing on hurdles debut at Southwell 12 days ago, losing touch back straight. Can only be watched.

Knew what was required when making a winning debut in tidy fashion in 6-runner event at Doncaster in March. Had something to find up in class but ran no sort of race even so following 8 months off at Cheltenham 3 weeks ago. Not one to write off now hurdling and another best guided by the betting.

Modest maiden on Flat. Big prices and little to shout about on first 2 hurdle runs but not seen to best effect (also caught eye of stewards) when fourth on qualifying run in a C&D maiden 6 weeks ago. Remains capable of better, not least in handicaps.

Built on debut promise when landing Worcester bumper (2m) in September and even better when following up in maiden hurdle over same C&D a month later. Didn't look at all out of place when fourth pitched into Grade 2 at Cheltenham since, fluffing his lines last. Hard to beat back in calmer waters.

GB.label: 13:15 Uttoxeter
GB.race: Carlsberg EBF Mares' 'National Hunt' Maiden Hurdle (Gbb Race) (Class 4) (Turf) 4YO to 6YO 2m 3f 207y Winner: £5,809 (7 runners)
GB.note: MALINA ROAD laid down solid foundations in a trio of bumper starts last winter, including success at listed level and with this increase in trip promising to suit now hurdling, she shades preference over Boombox who went agonisingly close to making a successful stable/hurdling debut at Worcester recently. Bumper scorer Kentford Legacy hails from a yard in form and also commands a second look, as does Port And Brandy.

runners.tf_comment: Placed on 3 completed starts in points and finished second only start in bumpers for S. Curling at Killarney in May. Changed hands for £110,000 thereafter and went agonisingly close to making a winning yard/hurdles debut at Worcester (2m) in October. Expected to build on that and one to consider.

£120,000 purchase after winning sole start in Irish points. Steady progress in 3 bumper starts, third at Ludlow (2m) in April but looked one for later on/handicaps over hurdles when fifth of 7 in a C&D mares novice in May. Had breathing operation and looks best watched after 6 months off.

Stepped up a little on her debut form for Richard Bandey when second of 8 in bumper at Catterick (2m, good) in March. Similar form when fourth of 7 in a bumper at this course on return in October and likely more will be needed if she's to feature now hurdling.

Scorpion mare from a good jumping family who overcame inexperience to make a winning debut in a Fontwell bumper (2¼m, good, 22/1) in May, going in snatches but ultimately well on top at finish. Very much the type to make her mark over hurdles with her stable amongst the winners.

Won completed start in Irish points and successful on 2 of her 3 starts in bumpers last winter, latterly a listed event at Market Rasen (17f) in January. Lost her unbeaten record conceding weight all round when third at Newbury in February but she's a bright prospect now hurdling over a longer trip.

Little impact in a pair of bumpers but she built on her hurdles debut fifth when third in mares maiden over this trip at Hereford in March. Faced a stiff task when fifth in listed company next time and whilst this less demanding, others still appeal much more.

Made the frame both starts in bumpers and upped in trip for her hurdles bow, she posted a fair effort when second of 7 in a C&D mares novice back in May. That form may not be as good as first impressions would imply but a repeat gives her sound claims of being in the mix again.

GB.label: 13:50 Uttoxeter
GB.race: Karina's 60th Birthday Celebration Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle (Class 5) (Turf) 3YO+ 1m 7f 168y Winner: £3,697 (12 runners)
GB.note: CHAMBERS is well treated on his Flat form and having won his latest start in that sphere, he's fancied to make a successful handicap hurdle debut. Arcon didn't immediately improve on his handicap bow but looks capable of making an impact in this sort of company, whilst Prince Phil can improve handicapping.

runners.tf_comment: Fairly useful stayer on Flat (stays 2m). Caught the eye of the stewards at Uttoxeter in July before not really taking to brush hurdles at Worcester on qualifying run later that month. Didn't immediately improve making handicap debut at this C&D (good) 41 days ago but likely still capable of more.
Placed on completed start in points but no solid form under Rules.

Fair winner on Flat (up to 2m) in 2025 for George Boughey. Still looked a bit rough around the edges when fourth on handicap debut at Worcester in June but was below that level there the following month. Others preferred back from a break.

No impact in starts over hurdles in May/June but he's a fair sort on the Flat and has won twice on the level since last seen over obstacles, including at Southwell late last month. Clearly has a workable opening mark on that form now back over hurdles.

Signs of ability on the Flat for Karl Burke but there have been very few positives to take from his efforts in this sphere so far, jumping awkwardly prior to pulling up on last month's handicap debut at Worcester.
Minor promise in bumpers last season but showed little in 3 starts over hurdles subsequently for Sarah-Jayne Davies. Worth betting check making handicap debut for new yard after 7 months off.
Runner-up both starts in Irish points but nothing to shout about over hurdles so far, pulled up after racing freely on last month's handicap debut.

Fair form when runner-up twice from 3 starts in French bumpers. Well below that level in a couple of starts over hurdles, for all he shaped a bit better than the bare result when sixth of 7 in novice hurdle (66/1) at Fontwell (19f, good to soft) 30 days ago. Makes handicap hurdle debut.

Shaped as if better for the run but still surpassed the form of a couple of low-key efforts in Plumpton handicaps when fourth of 9 in novice hurdle at Cartmel (17f, good) in August. Seemed to back that form up when fifth in a Sedgefield maiden last month but might need more back in a handicap.
Showed a bit on bumper debut and though he failed to make an impact in 3 quick qualifying runs in the spring, he appeals as one who should do better now handicapping after a 6-month break.

Showed a bit when hitting the frame in a Newton Abbot bumper in July. Looks to be being brought along with handicaps in mind over hurdles, not unduly punished when fourth of 6 in novice hurdle (50/1) at that same course (17f, good) 47 days ago. Makes handicap bow having since left David Pipe.

Showed a fair level of ability in 2 Irish bumpers for Stuart Crawford but has yet to better modest form over hurdles, finishing only eighth on March's 2m Warwick handicap debut with a tongue tie added (retained). Returns from 8 months off here.

GB.label: 14:25 Uttoxeter
GB.race: Eaton Hall Shooting Ground Mares' Handicap Chase (Gbb Race) (Class 4) (Turf) 4YO+ 1m 7f 214y Winner: £5,281 (4 runners)
GB.note: A trappy mares handicap which can go the way of the experienced IRISH CHORUS, who did well in this sphere last season and was unable to recover from a late blunder on her recent comeback. Lau And Shaz had a positive time of things over hurdles last campaign and should prove at least as good over fences, whilst Lady Tadita should also benefit from her initial experience chasing.

runners.tf_comment: Winless over hurdles but different story over fences, winning 3 handicaps around 2m last season. Another good effort when second at Warwick in May. Pitching for a place when making a serious error 3 out on return at Huntingdon earlier this month, and she makes appeal back against her own sex.

Debut bumper winner and looked an even better prospect when winning her first 2 starts over hurdles last season, before a good second in listed mares novice at Taunton in December. However, was tailed off at Huntingdon in February and looked in need of the experience on her recent C&D chase debut.

Back to her best when making a successful stable debut in Wincanton novice on Boxing Day. Led until crumpling on landing 4 out at Windsor prior to resuming winning ways at Hereford. Anchored by a double penalty at Taunton in April but she appeals as one who should make a chaser this season.

Scored over hurdles at Hexham in October and largely in good form subsequently, signing off for the campaign when a good second of 15 in 21f handicap at Newbury in March. Made the frame in a point and she's not without hope sent chasing after having a breathing operation during the summer.

GB.label: 15:00 Uttoxeter
GB.race: Hobgoblin Handicap Chase (Gbb Race) (Class 4) (Turf) 4YO+ 3m 10y Winner: £5,281 (8 runners)
GB.note: ORDEROFTHEDAY ought to relish this step back up in trip, and he's taken to make it 2 wins from 3 starts over fences. Kahavari will be suited by speed-favouring conditions and just edges Kalhandrion for next best.

runners.tf_comment: Had been knocking on the door prior to coming out on top in sprint finish in a 4-runner chase at Sandown (2½m) in April. Probably needed his reappearance at Wetherby last time. Back up in trip and entitled to do better in race that could develop into a relative test of speed.

Half-brother to Valadom (useful chaser for connections). Impressed when making all to double his tally at Exeter (3m, heavy) before running better than the beaten distance might suggest final start last season. Goes well fresh, though relatively untested under these conditions over fences.

Winning pointer/hurdler. Found plenty to make a successful chasing debut here (2½m) in May. Entitled to come on for last month's comeback at Perth (beaten 17 lengths). Sets the standard on the pick of his form and remains capable of better stepping back up in trip.

Successful sole outing in points. Well-backed second on debut at Chepstow in April. More professional than on return when runner-up in first-time visor here (2½m) latest. Opening mark demands more, but he looks the type who could improve for the step back up in trip/quick switch to fences.

Third sole start in Irish points. Clearly hasn't been easy to train since making an impressive winning start over hurdles in March 2024. Returns 23 months on from a modest chasing debut and is probably the stable second string.

Won sole start in bumpers. Progressed into a fairly useful stayer when completing a handicap hurdle double at Doncaster in December. Underlined that consistency isn't his strong suit with 2 subsequent runs last season. Claims on pick of his form, for all others look more obvious chasing types.

Flat-bred 5-y-o with a good course record. Went close to snapping a 2-year losing run over hurdles here (23f) in September. Race fitness on his side when only beaten by a stronger stayer in big-field handicap at Chepstow (3m) since. Makes belated chasing debut and others perhaps have more scope.

From a good jumping family. Picked up for £42,000 after placing in a couple of points. Fairly useful winner on handicap hurdle bow at Uttoxeter (2½m, heavy) penultimate start last season. Stable has had several ready to roll in recent weeks, and he looks first string on jockey bookings.

GB.label: 15:35 Uttoxeter
GB.race: 1664 Biere Open Nh Flat Race (Gbb Race) (Class 5) (Turf) 4YO to 5YO 1m 7f 168y Winner: £2,451 (12 runners)
GB.note: JIMMY GATZ is well worth another chance to build on his strong debut form having probably found testing conditions against him at Ffos Las when last seen (Flat bred). Bateleur went down fighting on his Rules debut at Sedgefield last month and his excellent attitude is sure to stand him in good stead again, while the selection's stablemate, Hannah's Kitchen, is the pick of the newcomers before market clues.

runners.tf_comment: €30,000 3-y-o, £6,000 5-y-o, Feel Like Dancing gelding. Half-brother to fair hurdler Kells Priory, stays 25f. Wears tongue strap for Rules debut and makes little appeal based on his pointing exploits.

€3,000 3-y-o, Tirwanako gelding. Successful on his only start in point bumpers and, having attracted support, produced a promising first effort under Rules when second at Sedgefield last month, going down fighting. Likely to be on the premises again with his attitude sure to stand him in good stead.

€68,000 3-y-o, Poet's Word gelding. Half-brother to fairly useful hurdler/useful chaser Classic Maestro. Dam unraced half-sister to 19f bumper winner/fairly useful hurdle winner up to 23f Present In Court. Wears tongue strap for debut and the market should offer up some clues.
Masterstroke gelding. Dam unraced half-sister to fairly useful hurdler/useful chaser (stayed 3¼m) Merry King. Bred more for stamina than speed and stable has an ordinary strike rate in bumpers.
€55,000 3-y-o, Blue Bresil gelding. Dam unraced sister to multiple bumper winner/useful hurdler (2m winner) The Model Kingdom. Highly respected on debut for excellent yard.

Son of The Grey Gatsby who shaped encouragingly when fourth of 7 in a warm Carlisle bumper (17f) on his debut in February. Not in the same form at Ffos Las but was probably unsuited by testing conditions and well worth another chance back from 8 months off.

Well backed and knew her job when making a winning debut in 9-runner bumper at Bangor (17f, good) in April, seeing off a pair with experience in a close finish. More needed now taking on the boys under a penalty, though.

Shaped well in coming from the back to beat all bar one in a Hereford bumper on debut last November. Showed similar form when fifth in a warmer race at Kempton 3 months later and must enter calculations returning from another absence.

€80,000 No Risk At All gelding. Dam, ran once on Flat in France, half-sister to French chaser (stayed 2¾m) Quolibet. Runner-up sole start in Irish points (Apr 2026) and is another to consider on this switch to Rules.

Masked Marvel gelding. Dam, French hurdler/chaser (17f-21f winner), sister to French hurdler/chaser (17f-23f winner) Utopia Dream and fairly useful 3m hurdle winner Jakar du Moulin. Needs a market check for a yard which has its fair share of success in this sphere.
Heeraat gelding. Half-brother to 2 winners, including fair hurdler Gms Prince, stays 2¾m. Dam 9f-1½m winner. Yard knows this family well.

£30,000 4-y-o, Order of St George gelding. Half-brother to French 2¼m hurdle winner Lascaux. Dam, French hurdler (2¼m winner), half-sister to French hurdler/chaser (15f-19f winner) Laskaline. Runner-up sole start in Irish points (May 2026).

GB.label: 12:13 Wetherby
GB.race: Boyle Sports Novices' Hurdle (Gbb Race) (Class 3) (Turf) 4YO+ 2m 3f 154y Winner: £8,169 (3 runners)
GB.note: LORIKO tasted success 4 times over hurdles for his top yard during the summer, reaching a near-useful level in the process and having shaped much better than the margin of defeat would imply on chase debut 11 days ago, he looks to have been found an excellent opportunity quickly reverting back to smaller obstacles. Irish raider Combs comfortably rates the chief threat with first-time blinkers applied.

runners.tf_comment: Got back on track to finally open his hurdle account in 2m Kilbeggan maiden on reappearance. Disappointed next 2 starts and whilst he wasn't seen to best effect when eighth in Down Royal handicap 2 weeks ago, he didn't convince with his jumping. Still, easily the lead threat to Loriko. Blinkers on.

Thrived for top yard this summer, winning 4 small-field hurdles, reaching a near-useful level in the process. Likely he'd have run close to that form but for losing his footing late on when beaten in a match on chase debut at Warwick (2m) 11 days ago and found an excellent opening back hurdling.

Fair maiden at best on Flat for A. Slattery (stays 10.5f) but offered little in 2 starts during the spring and it was a similar story sent hurdling returning for his new yard over 2m here 2 weeks ago. Passed over up in trip.

GB.label: 12:48 Wetherby
GB.race: Boyle Sports Back Yourself Handicap Hurdle (Class 3) (Turf) 3YO+ 2m 5f 56y Winner: £5,281 (6 runners)
GB.note: THE KALOOKI KID didn't go on from his return last season, but he reverts to hurdles from 11 lb below his chase mark and has had a breathing operation ahead of his reappearance. Representing a stable amongst the winners, he gets the vote ahead of Jericoacoara, who opened his account for his current yard when last seen in May.

runners.tf_comment: Won first 2 starts over hurdles for Dan Skelton but her form has gone the wrong way since, making handicap/stable debut when well held at Uttoxeter 15 days ago.

Had been shaping well for current yard with 3 placed efforts to start this year, before gaining a first British success in handicap at Kelso (23f) in May. Off 6 months but he's respected now that he's regained the winning thread.

Showed promise when making the frame 2 of 3 starts in maiden hurdles for Gordon Elliott earlier this year, fourth of 13 at Cork (23f) when last seen in April. One to note as he makes handicap/stable debut, especially if the market speaks in his favour.

Notched third win for Warren Greatrex in a Cartmel handicap in May last year. Pulled up in listed mares hurdle at Sandown on final outing of the campaign, but after 7 months off she possibly needed the run on stable debut when down the field at Cartmel in July. Off again since.

Useful chaser but didn't build on last season's reappearance in 3 subsequent outings, shaping as if amiss when pulled up at Ludlow in March. However, he returns having had a breathing operation and is on a handy mark back hurdling. Interesting with his yard going well.

After 4 months off, showed his first form in maiden hurdles when fourth of 16 at Roscommon (2½m) in August, the easy winner scoring again next time. Will need to find more again as he goes handicapping after 3 months off.

GB.label: 13:20 Wetherby
GB.race: Sebden Steel Celebrating 30 Years In Business Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (Gbb Race) (Class 3) (Turf) 4YO+ 1m 7f 36y Winner: £6,337 (4 runners)
GB.note: SPADESTEP produced a laboured effort at Carlisle when last seen, but he was a winner first time back (over hurdles) last season and this could be the time to catch him, especially with his yard in red-hot form. Le Beau Madrik came off second best in a match race with Florida Dreams just over a fortnight ago and is now much worse off at the weights, but that experience shouldn't have been lost on him and it's reasonable to believe he can reverse the form.

runners.tf_comment: A dual bumper/hurdles winner for Nicky Richards who accounted for reopposing Le Beau Madrik under a skilful ride in match race here (19f) just over a fortnight earlier. Meets that rival on much more favourable terms back in a handicap, so good chance of confirming the form.

Runner-up sole outing in bumpers and promising novice hurdler last season, winning 3 of his 4 starts. Came up short on his handicap bow in the Welsh Champion Hurdle and was undone by a less-than-fluent round of jumping when beaten ½-length by Florida Dreams on recent chasing debut. Should do better.

Won 5 of his first 6 completed starts over hurdles. Improved again when narrowly denied in a Haydock handicap (good to soft) in January but his form tailed off thereafter. Switches to the larger obstacles after 7 months off and should make a chaser.

Point/hurdles winner who was runner-up on his first 4 starts over fences last season, sure to have pushed the winner closer but for a jolting error at Newcastle (2m) in February. Laboured effort at Carlisle on final outing but returns with his yard amongst the winners. Has had a breathing operation.

GB.label: 13:55 Wetherby
GB.race: Boyle Sports Now Open In Wetherby Introductory' Hurdle (Gbb Race) (Class 2) (Turf) 4YO+ 2m Winner: £10,892 (4 runners)
GB.note: VELVET OUTLAW is pretty hard to oppose after finishing runner-up in a bumper on Rules debut. Yashin may still possess enough ability to chase him home.

runners.tf_comment: Fair sort on the Flat who bagged a pair of middle-distance handicaps this summer. Made the frame at Redcar when last seen but will likely need to improve significantly to make a winning hurdles debut.
Bred for the Flat and hit the frame all 3 starts in bumpers but made a disappointing start over hurdles when only twelfth of 13 in novice at Bangor (17f, good) on debut in April. Off 7 months.

Poet's Word gelding held every chance when fell sole outing in Irish points and made an encouraging start under Rules when second of 4 in bumper at Perth (2m, soft, evens) on 30 days ago. Looks the one to beat.
Smart Group 3 winner at his best on the Flat for Michael Bell but little show on the lest season, including making his debut for this yard at Galway in July. Debuts over hurdles in a weak race.

GB.label: 14:30 Wetherby
GB.race: Boyle Sports Handicap Chase (Gbb Race) (Class 3) (Turf) 4YO+ 2m 3f 85y Winner: £7,922 (5 runners)
GB.note: Likeable veteran TOMMY'S OSCAR looks the most solid option in a tricky race for betting purposes. Palamon is likely to have a say if on a going day, with similar comments applying to 3-time C&D winner Geryville.

runners.tf_comment: Hit-and-miss type. Landed C&D wins (both on heavy) in each of the last 2 seasons. Left his reappearance behind when rallying to finish second in this corresponding event (soft) 12 months ago. May follow suit on the back of last month's comeback, for all he'd probably have preferred more rain.

Veteran who clearly isn't the force he was for Olly Murphy. Didn't build on the minor promise of his stable debut when well beaten in the Summer Plate in July. Hard to be confident he'll capitalise on slipping mark following further 4 months off.

Easy winner at Southwell before looking unlucky not to defy a penalty behind a borderline useful one at Plumpton last month. Ran well in first-time blinkers (despite again hinting at temperament) when 1¼-length third over C&D latest. Can go well for yard's 10-lb claimer, if headgear has same effect.

Created a good impression when making it 2 wins from 3 over fences at Haydock in February. Clearly wasn't 100% final start last season (since undergone another breathing operation). Relatively inexperienced claimer takes over and cannot be discounted if back on song (good record fresh).

Consistent sort who readily won a veterans race at Carlisle in March. Better for his comeback when going close off this mark in a similar event at Market Rasen last time. Has the least to prove in this field and may get his head in front on a rare start in class 3 company.

GB.label: 15:05 Wetherby
GB.race: Colin Baldwin Memorial Handicap Hurdle (Class 3) (Turf) 3YO+ 2m Winner: £5,281 (5 runners)
GB.note: Hat-trick-seeking CENTURION'S SISTER could still be ahead of her mark and is taken to defy a rise in grade. Roarin' Success and Filibustering both look solid dangers in a tight handicap.

runners.tf_comment: Much improved when impressively making it 2-2 in cheekpieces at this course (2½m) last time. Return to 2m unlikely to harm given her zestful style, and she may get the run of race if again allowed to stride on. Looks capable of defying a rise in grade on her hat-trick bid.

Fair sort who convincingly got off the mark at Worcester (2m) in August. Better than he's been able to show both starts since, latterly under a change of tactics off a quick turnaround at Fontwell (2¼m). Freshened up by top yard and isn't discounted back over 2m on second handicap start.

Landed a third successive hurdle success in emphatic fashion at Cartmel in late-June. Well-held eighth in Welsh Champion Hurdle prior to resuming winning ways back in calmer waters over C&D last time. Off a career-high mark, however, he should go well again in another small-field event.

Made most of a good opportunity to get off the mark at Fairyhouse (2½m). No impact couple starts since falling on handicap bow (going well at time), weak in the betting on return at Ballinrobe (2¾m). No surprise to see him back down in trip 9 weeks on from that headstrong display.

Fairly useful Flat performer. Well backed when completing a double at Stratford in July. Solid efforts in defeat all 4 outings subsequently, finishing a length second to a progressive one at Newcastle (17f) latest. Similar performance should see her firmly in the mix here.

GB.label: 15:40 Wetherby
GB.race: Boyle Sports Conditional Jockeys' Handicap Chase (Gbb Race) (Class 4) (Turf) 4YO+ 3m 45y Winner: £4,225 (6 runners)
GB.note: SLANEY OPERA has made a positive start for his new trainer, scoring at Uttoxeter in October and beaten only by an improver over C&D last time, so he is taken to resume winning ways. Safe Destination returned to form when third to the selection on his reappearance and is the pick for second, ahead of Camarrate.

runners.tf_comment: Bred for the Flat but was a fair winner over hurdles and has made a positive start over fences in 2 handicaps at Uttoxeter, seeing things out well upped to 3m when ½-length second of 8 to Slaney Opera last month. Can make his presence felt.

Made a winning handicap/chase debut at Market Rasen in February last year but raced only twice in 2025/26, well beaten on second start over fences in March. Possibly needed the run over hurdles at Huntingdon 13 days ago, though he has something to find back chasing.

Bumper winner who matched his hurdles form at the first attempt over fences when second in 14-runner handicap at Bangor in April, though again hung left under pressure. Task is now to build on his chasing debut effort after 7 months off.

Proved better than ever when landing a 3¼m Chepstow handicap on second start last season. Ended the campaign with a couple of poor runs, but he bounced back when 4 lengths third of 8 to Slaney Opera at Uttoxeter on his return. Enters calculations.

Making first start for current trainer, got back to winning ways at Uttoxeter last month and ran at least as well when second of 4 over this C&D 2 weeks ago, clear of the rest. Major player with more still to offer for this yard.

Rejuvenated by the switch to blinkers last season, capitalising on a reduced mark at Newcastle (2½m) in December and following up at Carlisle in February. However, he found things tougher in a higher grade at Carlisle when last seen 7 months ago. Back in cheekpieces for his return.

GB.label: 12:20 Windsor
GB.race: A1r Services LTD Mares' Maiden Hurdle (Gbb Race) (Class 4) (Turf) 3YO+ 2m Winner: £5,446 (16 runners)
GB.note: This looks between TI'MAMZEL and Jem's Lilly with the former taken to make a winning start over hurdles having impressed in bumpers.

runners.tf_comment: Hasn't offered much since her debut bumper fourth at Wincanton, including starting out for this yard on return.
Half-sister to fairly useful hurdler Top Jimmy and bumper winner/fair 2m hurdle winner Sir Hobnob. Dam bumper winner. Green when mid-field in bumper at Chepstow 5 weeks ago.

Fair form shown in Irish bumpers and has made an encouraging start to her hurdles career for Harry Derham, again making the frame when second of 16 in Kempton novice when last seen in February. Sets a clear standard with hood applied on return.
Half-sister to fair hurdler Time Interval. Long-standing maiden on the Flat (stays 11f).

€20,000 3-y-o, £105,000 4-y-o, Beaumec De Houelle filly. Dam, 17f-3m hurdle/chase winner, half-sister to useful chaser (stayed 3½m) Chef d'Oeuvre. Runner-up sole outing in Irish points in March and seemed unsuited by the emphasis on speed when fourth in Uttoxeter novice 2 weeks ago.

€32,000 3-y-o, €30,000 4-y-o, Maxios filly. Dam unraced half-sister to bumper winner/fairly useful hurdler (stays 3m) Park Princess out of bumper/2m hurdle winner Reine Angevine. Runner-up both completed starts in Irish points (latest May 2026).
Sumbal filly out of an unraced sister to useful hurdler/chaser Golden Taipan. Well held in Fakenham bumper. Tongue strap on.
Modest winner on Flat who's probably best watched on hurdles bow.
Aided by the run of the race winning Plumpton bumper in March. Well held in maiden hurdles 6 months apart and perhaps one for handicaps later on.
Planteur filly. Half-sister to fairly useful hurdler/fair chase winner Na Caith Tobac. Dam 1m/9f winner. Well held in bumper at Plumpton in March.

Runner-up on second of 2 starts in Irish points and had a bit up her sleeve when winning a 5-runner bumper at Wincanton on Rules debut in April. Underwhelming sent hurdling next 2 starts 5 months apart, though, and has since left Harry Fry.

€23,000 3-y-o, Poet's Word filly. Half-sister to useful hurdler Flemcara and useful hurdler/chaser Quinta Do Mar. Dam 2m-3m hurdle/chase winner. Fourth on both starts in Irish points. Always behind in Ascot bumper.
Gentlewave mare. Half-sister to bumper winner Blue Betty. Dam, ran twice in bumpers, half-sister to smart hurdler/useful chaser Bitofapuzzle.

€105,000 3-y-o by No Risk At All. Half-sister to fairly useful French hurdler A L'abord'az. Dam, ran once over hurdles, sister to useful French hurdler/chaser Al Bucq. Showed plenty in bumpers last season, winning a couple of listed events. Has bags of scope and interesting hurdling debutant.
Gentlewave half-sister to fairly useful chaser Pure Carbon. Placed all 3 starts in bumpers with her debut being her best effort. Tongue strap fitted for hurdles bow.
Little solid form on the Flat and offered little tried over hurdles last time.

GB.label: 12:55 Windsor
GB.race: Freight Movement Same Day Novices' Handicap Chase (Gbb Race) (Class 4) (Turf) 4YO+ 2m 4f 42y Winner: £7,393 (6 runners)
GB.note: With the benefit of an encouraging comeback/chasing debut under her belt, SCAVENGERS REIGN looks the percentage call for the excellent James Owen Team. Le Tiep's Sacre is likely to be a serious threat if ready to roll on first start over fences.

runners.tf_comment: Point/hurdle winner who walked over on return/chasing debut. Best run in handicaps when fairly useful fourth (beaten 3½ lengths) at Uttoxeter in March. Races off 2 lb lower mark under capable claimer here, and returns with yard typically going well.

Made a winning start for Olly Murphy in maiden hurdle at Fakenham (2½m, soft). Shaped with encouragement over 3m at Uttoxeter in March (pulled up in handicaps either side). Likely to find this too sharp on chasing debut/return.

Fair bumper winner who flattered to deceive in maiden hurdles. Underwent a breathing operation prior to making little impact on reappearance/chasing debut (well behind Scavengers Reign when falling at the last). Trip remains a question mark for this weak-finishing 6-y-o.

Lightly-raced 5-y-o. Beat a fairly useful type in likeable fashion to win Fontwell maiden hurdle. Shaped promisingly when 3¼-length fifth in a solid race on return/handicap bow in March. On a good mark for chasing debut (should make a better chaser), for all he seemingly isn't the easiest to train.

Third sole start in Irish points. Had some solid-looking placed form as novice hurdler. Not given hard time when his chance had gone at Chepstow (following a breathing operation) latest start in April. Opening mark demands more, though he looks the type to make a chaser.

Placed sole start in points. Justified heavy support to get off the mark in mares maiden hurdle at Wetherby on Boxing Day. Shaped well when much-improved second on chasing debut at Huntingdon on return, pulling clear with stablemate. Again takes on the boys and every chance she goes one better.

GB.label: 13:25 Windsor
GB.race: Fitzdares Telephone & Text Betting Handicap Hurdle (Class 3) (Turf) 4YO+ 3m Winner: £13,202 (15 runners)
GB.note: A big field but there should be plenty more to come from KILDINAN PRINCE this season and with the return to 3m in his favour, he has a lot going for him. Tzarmix and Thank You Ma'am look solid rivals, while Doctor on Call may also raise his game on reappearance.

runners.tf_comment: Veteran who posted a fairly useful effort when beaten 7½ lengths in Pertemps Final in March. Has looked on the slide since, offering very little in 3 starts for this stable. Change of headgear tried.

Modest stayer on the Flat who was found a weak handicap to get off the mark over hurdles at Uttoxeter in May. Added to tally from lowly mark on the level last month before blotting his copybook at Catterick. Looks up against it.

Bumper winner who crucially jumped better than previously when opening his account over hurdles in 7-runner handicap at Uttoxeter (23f) in May. Seemed anchored by 7 lb rise when second in 3-runner contest on Southwell return 44 days ago but this 4-y-o remains unexposed over this trip.

Bumper winner who looked a work in progress over hurdles last season for all he did sign off with a victory in a 3-runner maiden at Ludlow in February (3m). Left Paul Nicholls but joined another very capable yard and cheekpieces are on for handicap debut.
Dual bumper winner who scored twice over hurdles in 2024. Off since November of that year, though and while his stable is in good form, his well-being has to be taken on trust.

Runner-up in Tipperary maiden in May, and having changed hands for €40,000, improved when filling the same position in Ascot novice on stable debut in February. Didn't have to get near that level to see off 2 vastly inferior rivals at Exeter soon after and he retains plenty of potential this season.

Lightly-raced 6-y-o who jumped well when off the mark in a 3m handicap at Ffos Las in February (heavy). Didn't back that up at Uttoxeter the following month but promising enough return to the track at former venue when third 3 weeks ago.

Opened his hurdles account in a heavy-ground handicap at Wincanton (2½m) in January, Pipped in a ding-dong battle with another progressive one at Hereford next time but he didn't fully see out 3m on his first attempt at Cheltenham, albeit it was his reappearance.

Did well for Alastair Ralph last season, winning at Ascot a year ago and Warwick in March. Was going with enthusiasm when falling in a handicap hurdle at Hereford (2½m, good) in May and having changed yards, he was well prepared to score at Newton Abbot 4 weeks ago. 3m is unknown territory.

Enjoyed a very productive 2025/26 season, winning for the third time at Wincanton (25f) in March. Didn't do a lot wrong at Bangor a month later and lot depends on whether he's primed for this reappearance.

Dual hurdles winner who made a successful reappearance/chasing debut at Fontwell this time last year. Unable to continue the good work over both sets of obstacles since, though he stuck to his task pretty well on first try over 3m last month. Cheekpieces on.

Beat a progressive one when successful at Musselburgh a year ago and produced a career best to follow up at Bangor in April. Shade unlucky at latter track 3 weeks ago, looking sure to play a big part in the finish until he was hampered.

Smooth-travelling sort who landed his third success of last season at Kempton on Boxing Day. Shaped well when fourth from 6 lb higher at Ascot soon after but off since and he's not really crying out for 3m.

Fairly useful stayer who again gave his running when 9½-length second at Chepstow on return last month. Also nothing wrong with latest fourth in a Pertemps qualifier 3 weeks ago and this likeable type is sure to give it another good go from the front.

Strong-staying type who was suited by the return to positive tactics when doubling his tally for the yard on last month's reappearance at Chepstow. Kept the mistakes down on that occasion and 5 lb rise may well be within range if doing so again.

GB.label: 14:00 Windsor
GB.race: Listen Live to Track Radio Mares' Handicap Hurdle (Class 5) (Turf) 4YO+ 2m 4f Winner: £3,697 (12 runners)
GB.note: INDEPENDENT LADY shaped well on her return when second at Uttoxeter last month, beaten only by a fellow improver, and she can build on that effort to double her tally. The main danger could be Barafundle Bay, who arrives on the back of a breakthrough success over hurdles, ahead of Mavis Pike.

runners.tf_comment: Successful over 11.5f here on the Flat and has fared better than previously over hurdles on her last 2 starts, winning a Hereford handicap last month albeit fortunate having been left clear at the last. Still merits consideration now that she's going the right way.
Remains a maiden but possibly needed the run after 5 months off when fourth of 6 in handicap at Fontwell (19f) 24 days ago. Mark has eased further as a result, though more needed to take advantage.

Fared better than previously under Rules when 2¾ lengths second of 3 in maiden hurdle at Exeter (2¾m) in March, though was no match for the odds-on winner. Never a threat after 7 months off when fourth of 7 in handicap at Ffos Las (2m) 16 days ago. Cheekpieces applied.

All 3 career victories at Plumpton, the latest when making all for a comfortable success in February. After 6 months off, shaped as if as good as ever when third of 7 at the same course in October, though she remains 2 lb above her last winning mark.
Some encouragement on her first start over hurdles but hasn't gone on from that performance, ridden patiently making her handicap debut at Huntingdon 13 days ago and unseating rider 4 out.

Much improved upped to 2½m when making a winning handicap debut at Hereford in March. Failed to land the odds there next time, but after 6 months off she resumed her progress when second of 10 at Uttoxeter (2m) in October. Major player back up in trip.

Won pair of 2m handicap hurdles at Fakenham in 2024/25 but well held both completed starts over fences. However, reverted to hurdles she got back on track when second of 6 at Hereford 19 days ago. Back up in trip and could be in the mix from a handy mark.

Free-going type who produced her best effort when runner-up in handicap at Fontwell (2¾m) in May. Lesser effort at the same course (19f) the following month, though her yard is going well ahead of her return.

Placed in Irish points prior to making the frame in a 2m Worcester maiden on hurdling debut in September. Well held both subsequent outings, so she has something to find as she goes up in distance for handicap bow.
Without a win for Garrett James Power in Ireland and little promise starting off for this yard when pulled up in handicap hurdle at Worcester in August. Regular tongue strap now back on.

Tailed off in a bumper and didn't go with much promise in 3 starts over hurdles for Fergal O'Brien. After 8 months off, failed to last home on stable debut when fourth of 6 in handicap at Ffos Las (2½m) 16 days ago, but this run should reveal more.

Stepped forward from last season's return when opening hurdles account in a Leicester handicap (2m) a year ago. Hasn't kicked on from that effort, though, possibly failing to stay when mid-field at Chepstow (19f) in April. Off 7 months since back in blinkers/tongue strap.
NON RUNNER.

GB.label: 14:35 Windsor
GB.race: Join Fitzdares for a Personal Service Handicap Chase (Gbb Race) (Class 4) (Turf) 4YO+ 2m 6f 50y Winner: £5,281 (8 runners)
GB.note: KING CALIFET went the right way in his 3 starts over fences last season, opening his chasing account at Newbury in March with the runner-up winning both races since. He is open to further progress on his return and is fancied to follow up, with Jet Smart feared most from only 1 lb above his last winning mark. Dangerous Touch completes the shortlist.

runners.tf_comment: Still looking for a first win over fences, but in blinkers he shaped best when second of 4 at Huntingdon (3m) in March. Filled the same position at Market Rasen next time and he can make another bold bid on his return (has had a breathing operation) back in cheekpieces with tongue strap added.

Showed ability on hurdles debut but below that level next 2 starts. Got back on track when fourth of 5 on handicap/chase debut at Chepstow (2m) in April, chance-ending mistake 2 out, though was pulled up at Warwick next time. Has work to do after 6 months off (has had a breathing operation).

Fair maiden hurdler who matched that form at the first time of asking over fences when third of 5 in handicap at Wincanton (25f) in February, despite suffering interference. Task is now to build on that effort after 6 months off. Has had a breathing operation with tongue strap fitted.

Prolific winner in points who was successful on first 2 chase starts last season. Good efforts when runner-up on first 3 outings of the current campaign, before lesser efforts the last twice. However, no surprise to see him bounce back with good-value claimer on board.

Not the most straightforward (finds little) but had been proving consistent in defeat last season, including when runner-up at this course (2½m) on New Year's Day. Ran poorly both subsequent outings, though he's capable of running well fresh (has had a breathing operation).

Successful on first of 3 starts over hurdles and progressed with each outing over fences last season, again looking an assured jumper when winning 11-runner Newbury handicap in March. Form from last time has worked out very well and he's a strong contender on his return.

Remains a maiden but in first-time cheekpieces he soon left behind a lesser effort when third of 5 in handicap chase at Plumpton (2½m) in February. Faced a tougher ask up in grade when fifth of 8 at Fontwell in March, though his mark has at least eased ahead of his return (goes without headgear).

Maiden over hurdles but confirmed the promise of his chasing debut when winning a Ffos Las handicap (21f) in May. Followed up at the same course (3m) later the same month, but has disappointed both starts since returning from a break.

GB.label: 15:10 Windsor
GB.race: Cutler and Gross Handicap Hurdle (Class 3) (Turf) 3YO+ 2m Winner: £13,202 (11 runners)
GB.note: Useful Flat performer ANNIVERSARY has made a sound start over hurdles and his opening mark may underestimate him. This does look competitive, though, with Misterdoc and Moves Like Mason heading the dangers.

runners.tf_comment: Useful on Flat (stays 14.5f) and was well prepared to make a winning hurdling debut for new yard at Fontwell last month. Beaten only by a smart prospect at Plumpton under a penalty since and opening mark is potentially a lenient one, especially given Flat form.
Completed a 4-timer in early 2025 but has been below that level for a while now and offered no encouragement both starts for this yard. Has had breathing operation since last run.
Consistent sort who completed a double at Musselburgh on New Year's Day. Typically ran with credit in defeat since but he's summed up by his current mark.
Became temperamental for Hobbs & White yard and showed nothing starting out for this yard at Chepstow after 5 months off.
Heavy-ground novice winner at Exeter in February and similar form when placed in handicaps at Chepstow and Cheltenham both starts this season.

French bumper winner. Looked a good prospect for this yard when readily bagging a pair of 2m novice hurdles at Ludlow/Perth. Stepped up again when runner-up at Newton Abbot on handicap bow/return, beaten only by a rival well-in on old form who got first run. Remains of interest off same mark.

Caught the eye in 2 runs over hurdles in the space of a week in 2025. Gambled on when too free at Huntingdon in April and showed what he's capable of when a much-improved second on handicap bow at Uttoxeter on return. This is tougher but he may have more to offer.
Stylish winner of similar event over C&D nearly 2 years ago. Lightly raced since but is fit from the Flat and was a good third of 4 in Grade 2 at Wincanton on return last season.

Won newcomers hurdle at Pau last Christmas for J. Delaunay but well below that level all 3 starts for current yard (rider given a 14-day suspension for failing to take all reasonable and permissible measures to obtain the best possible placing on penultimate start).
Dual 2m novice winner last season and improved again when impressive winner of Stratford handicap 4 weeks ago. Raised 7 lb but she had a bit in hand and has the makings of a useful handicapper.

Fit from the Flat (won at Epsom) when making a winning handicap debut in this sphere at Newbury 9 days ago despite not enjoying the clearest run in the straight. Good chance he has more to offer over hurdles providing his jumping holds up.

GB.label: 15:45 Windsor
GB.race: Download the Fitzdares App 'Junior' Nh Flat Race (Gbb Race) (Class 5) (Turf) 3YO only 2m Winner: £2,451 (9 runners)
GB.note: NEW ADDINGTON BOY makes some appeal on paper for a yard going well at present, so he's put forward as the answer before market clues. Noe Le Dun, Waverley and Folkham are a trio of others to monitor closely in the betting in a race where only one has experience.

runners.tf_comment: €6,000 3-y-o, Siyouni gelding. Half-brother to 3 winners on Flat, including 9f/9.4f winner in France Volcano. Dam ran once on Flat in France. Has already undergone a breathing operation ahead of debut.
Jack Hobbs gelding. Dam (b70) ran twice in bumpers. Others make more appeal on paper.
Roseman gelding who is a half-brother to 3 winners. Dam 1½m winner. Needs a close look in the betting with Ben Jones a positive jockey booking.

€40,000 3-y-o, Blue Bresil gelding. Half-brother to 3 winners, including useful hurdler/smart chaser Enniskerry and useful hurdler/smart chaser Good Boy Bobby (winner up to 3m). More stoutly bred than most of his rivals.
A cheap purchase who was probably flattered when 3¾ lengths fifth of 8 in bumper at Huntingdon on last month's debut. Wouldn't be sure to build on that.
Frontiersman gelding. Half-brother to 1½m winner Everest. Dam (h103) 2m hurdle winner, also 7f-1¼m winner who stayed 13.5f on Flat. Yard going well and one to consider on debut.
Bathyrhon gelding. Brother to French hurdler/chaser Italiaana Le Dun, and half-brother to 2 winners, including fairly useful hurdle winner around 2m Romancero Le Dun. One to note in the betting.
Churchill gelding. Dam 1m-1½m winner. Yard gets the odd bumper winner and he should be suited by the emphasis on speed.
Camelot gelding. Dam ran twice on Flat. One for shortlist on debut given sharp test should suit on breeding. Wears hood.

GB.label: 12:35 Cheltenham
GB.race: Citipost Amateur Jockeys' Handicap Chase (Gbb Race) (Class 3) (Turf) 4YO+ 3m 1f Winner: £12,832 (10 runners)
GB.note: Despite losing his unbeaten record over fences, LITTLE LEDGEND emerged with plenty of credit when third in a similar amateur riders' handicap over C&D 3 weeks ago. In a change of headgear he's marginally preferred to Herakles Westwood and Transmission, both of whom have previous in this race.

runners.tf_comment: Won 3m Southwell handicap chase in March 2025. Didn't fire in 3 runs last season and again folded alarmingly on last month's reappearance.

Thorough stayer who finally got off the mark in 10-runner handicap chase at Down Royal (3¼m, good to soft) in May. Brushed aside over hurdles on return from a break but much more like it when third at Down Royal 2 weeks ago, 5 lengths behind Dinoland.

Much improved for his current yard when landing handicap chases at Downpatrick (3m) and Tramore (2¾m) in May. Failed to complete the hat-trick switched to hurdling after a break but confirmed he's still in top form over the larger obstacles when second at Down Royal 2 weeks ago.

Successful over 25f at Cheltenham on New Year's Day before finding the spring festivals a shade too competitive. Runner-up in this race 12 months ago and leading amateur rider booked. Has to be of interest.

Quick off the mark for new yard when winning at Worcester and at Uttoxeter earlier this season. Kept busy since and got back on track after a couple of subdued efforts when placed the last twice, latterly over C&D 3 weeks ago fitted with a tongue tie for the first time.

Has taken well to chasing this season, winning 23f handicaps at Killarney in July and August before finding another jolt of improvement for latest success at Roscommon. Shaped as though still in form when fourth at Down Royal 2 weeks ago, though was behind 2 re-opposing rivals.

Has quickly made up into a better chaser than hurdler, winning a pair of Worcester handicaps in August/September. Lost his unbeaten record but shaped well when third over C&D under this rider 3 weeks ago and in a change of headgear, he remains of interest.

Won 3m handicap hurdles at Wexford and Bellewstown in 2025. Has made a promising start over fences for Denis Hogan, not always fluent but still finished runner-up in the Cork National (3½m) 2 weeks ago, Unexposed as a stayer.

Lightly raced for his age and enhanced good strike rate over fences in 7-runner handicap chase at Carlisle (25f) in February, staying on well. Could manage only fifth at Sandown a month later and mark looks about right (sixth in last year's renewal).

Back to form with a bang during the spring, winning Edinburgh National and solid efforts in Sussex National/Bet365 Gold Cup. Always on the back foot following an early mistake returned to chasing at Ascot 2 weeks ago and better expected in a change of headgear. Won this from 2 lb lower in 2024.

Has never stood much racing but having left Olly Murphy for £16,000 in May, he showed much more than previous 2 attempts over fences when second of 7 at Ffos Las a month ago (3½m). This is a deeper race, though.

Irish point winner who scored twice in staying handicap hurdles last season and was going the right way in the spring. Should make his mark over fences at some point but both starts last month fairly low key. Could hardly be in better hands though as he goes back up in distance.

GB.label: 13:10 Cheltenham
GB.race: JCB Triumph Trial Juvenile Hurdle (Registered As the Prestbury Juvenile Hurdle) (Grade 2) (Gbb Race) (Class 1) (Turf) 3YO only 2m 87y Winner: £47,552 (9 runners)
GB.note: James Owen has won 2 of the last 3 renewals and has a good chance of adding to that tally with CHARLES DARNAY, who looks another very useful juvenile for connections after his listed win at Wetherby. Irish challengers Atomic City and Admiral Will Brown were both impressive when making winning debuts in this sphere so rate as serious threats.

runners.tf_comment: Flat winner for this yard and made a winning start over hurdles in good style fitted with a tongue strap at Down Royal (a race won by subsequent Grade 1 winners Wodhooh and Mange Tout in recent years) 2 weeks ago, leading on bridle between 3 and 2 out. Needs considering.
Flat maiden winner on heavy ground in the spring and looked potentially useful when making a successful hurdling debut with a fair amount in hand in Cork maiden 5 weeks ago. On the shortlist.

Progressive winner on the Flat and overcame inexperience (took time to warm to his task) to make a successful start in this sphere in listed event at Wetherby 2 weeks ago. That is just about the best form on offer and he rates an exciting prospect.

Maiden winner on the Flat in Ireland for Jessica Harrington. Progressed as expected from his gentle introduction to hurdling when 5¾ lengths fourth to Charles Darnay in listed event at Wetherby but has work to do to turn around the form with that one. Headgear on (well held when tried on Flat).

Progressive form in the spring for Mme M. Pineda, winning at Compiegne on third start. Changed hands for €150,000 after and only just failed to make a winning start for this yard at Market Rasen 3 weeks ago, an error 2 out and his awkwardness under pressure costing him. Headgear now applied.
Flat winner who's out of a half-sister to very smart hurdler/smart chase winner (2m-19f winner) Grey Shot, but this looks a very tall order on hurdles bow.

Useful stayer on the Flat but will need to jump with a lot more confidence in order to reach similar heights over hurdles given the manner of his hurdles debut win at Wetherby last month, rallying to lead close home after some iffy jumps. Yard also saddles Charles Darnay.
